title: Preflight: detect GPU SKU and warn on unsupported driver/CUDA for selected profile pack version
author: Ethan Park
description:
Context

As part of the hardware tuning profiles pack rollout (runtime-1.22) we’ve seen bring-up issues on early B200 nodes and a non-trivial amount of driver/CUDA variance in Private installs. When the runtime selects a profile based on SKU + driver/CUDA, mismatches can look like “random perf regressions” (kernel fallbacks, lower throughput) or instability (allocator behavior, OOM/fragmentation risk) and they’re hard to triage from customer reports.

This PR adds a preflight step to the Private installer to:
- Detect GPU SKU(s) on the node (H100 / B200 / L40S where possible).
- Detect NVIDIA driver version and CUDA runtime version (as reported by nvidia-smi).
- Validate the combination against the selected profile pack version’s compatibility matrix.
- Emit a clear warning with remediation steps (upgrade/downgrade driver, choose a supported profile pack version, or explicitly override).

We intentionally start with WARN-only by default to avoid bricking existing installs; we support an opt-in strict mode for customers who want to fail fast.

What changed

1) GPU + driver/CUDA detection
- New preflight probe that shells out to nvidia-smi and parses:
  - GPU product name (used for SKU mapping)
  - Driver Version
  - CUDA Version
- Handles multi-GPU nodes; we report per-unique SKU present.
- If detection fails (no nvidia-smi, non-NVIDIA env), we keep going and emit an informational message.

2) Compatibility validation (profile pack)
- Added a small, versioned compatibility map bundled with the installer (generated from the profile pack metadata we already publish internally).
- The installer reads the user-selected profile pack version (or “auto”) and checks:
  - SKU supported
  - driver_min/driver_max bounds (where defined)
  - cuda_min/cuda_max bounds (where defined)
- Output includes:
  - Active profile pack version requested
  - Detected {sku, driver, cuda}
  - Recommended remediation

3) Strict mode
- New flag: --enforce-gpu-compat
  - When set, the installer will fail the preflight phase if a mismatch is detected.
  - This is intended for regulated / locked-down environments where we prefer deterministic, supported behavior.

4) Installer report + logs
- Preflight results are included in the final installer report bundle as gpu_compat.json (so support can request it).
- Logs are structured and include fields: sku, driver_version, cuda_version, profile_pack_version, compat_status.

Why warnings (not hard fail) by default

We have a long tail of Private customers with fixed golden images and change control. Failing upgrades would create an urgent support event. The warning gives customers enough information to plan remediation, and strict mode is available for teams who want it.

Testing

- Unit tests cover:
  - parsing nvidia-smi output variants (different spacing + multiple GPUs)
  - version comparison and bounds checks
  - SKU mapping (H100 SXM/PCIe naming variants, L40S naming)
- Manual:
  - Verified on a local runner with NVIDIA driver installed
  - Verified “no nvidia-smi” path (container-only environments)

Release / follow-ups

- This PR does not change any runtime behavior directly; it is installer-only.
- Follow-up (separate PR): surface the warning in the UI/TTY step summary with a short “copy/paste” remediation block.

Refs
- ENG-4928 (B200 bring-up checklist)
- ENG-4922 (compatibility gate in schema/selection)
- Slack: eng-runtime B200 bring-up thread (driver mismatch errors) + SRE request for hard gates in Private where possible.
commits: preflight: add gpu compat probe (nvidia-smi parsing + sku mapping)
compat: bundle profile pack compatibility matrix and validator
installer: add --enforce-gpu-compat flag and report output
tests: parsing fixtures + version bounds checks
conversation:
Quentin Harris (review): Can we ensure the version comparison works for “535.161.07” style driver versions and doesn’t treat them as semver with missing components?

Ethan Park (author): Good catch. I added a driver-specific parser that normalizes to [major, minor, patch] ints and compares lexicographically. Added fixtures for 535.161.07 and 550.54.14.

Neha Kapoor (review): Please make sure the default behavior is warning-only. We can’t fail upgrades unexpectedly for existing Private customers.

Ethan Park (author): Agreed. Default remains WARN; strict mode only behind --enforce-gpu-compat. Also updated docs to reflect this.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Can we include the selected profile_pack_version in the report bundle? Support will need it when a customer says “we pinned X”.

Ethan Park (author): Done. The report now includes profile_pack_version and a compat_status enum. Also included the remediation string we print to console.

Rafael Mendes (review): The warning message should be actionable. Suggest: “Detected B200 + driver 535.x; profile pack v1.1 requires >= 550.x; either upgrade driver or pin profile pack v1.0”.

Ethan Park (author): Updated formatting to include exact bounds and the nearest known-good version from the matrix when available.

Connor O'Brien (review): Any impact on release train / backport?

Ethan Park (author): Low risk; installer-only. If we need to backport, it’s a clean cherry-pick (no runtime deps).

Approvals:
